results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec
All 63 aligned outline summaries state the controlling idea of their spec paragraph in spec order; the five callouts are unaligned preview units.

results.draft_locus: The Tracking Plan: The Schema Nobody Can Recall ¶5
results.quote: Two design rules follow from the table.
results.finding: The unit defines the common envelope and then states two design rules (server-side facts, keep impressions) that the draft itself derives from the core-events table, not from the envelope; the outliner read two ideas. The spec's controlling idea for p19 bundles the envelope and the two rules into one paragraph, so the split has to start in the spec.

Every table is introduced by a sentence saying what it shows or followed by one interpreting it (contacts table, six outputs + 'The table is the argument', three forms, core events, layers, quality controls, storage options, ownership matrix, card + 'Each row closes an argument', replay + 'The headline was', regimes, trade-offs, verticals); quotations (Adevinta 2024, Armbrust, Strategic Report, Dehghani) and statistics (Artemis, Meilleurs Agents/Scout24, logging cost, EUR 21M) are each followed by what they show. Figures 1, 3, 4 and 5 are not named in the adjacent prose; their numbered captions (not visible in units.json) are assumed to carry the explanation.

All declared transitions are expressed or clearly implied at their boundaries. Weakest: the scene section opens in narrative without a linking sentence (the roadmap's last sentence announces it); p27 'For a marketplace group the decision is less...' relies on its subheading for the sequence from gate to storage; p51 states the problem_solution link only in its closing sentence and p52's opening.

results.quote: Part VI priced, billed and tested against contact counts, and [[web-and-seo-architecture]] steered Tradeyard on organic contacts; this chapter makes "contact" mean the same thing in every brand.
results.finding: flow-A 3a: 'breaks the starts-from / works-back-to pair; had to re-read.' The bridge sentence sits between 'It starts from what a listing marketplace needs to know' and 'It works back to the contracts', splitting the paragraph's own sequence. The spec's bridge content is fine; its placement inside the sentence pair is a prose choice.

results.quote: Three of its layers hold **data products**, datasets a named team owns and publishes; their owners follow the rule in the next section.
results.finding: flow-A 3d: 'three new terms and a forward pointer; ... payoff feels distant.' flow-B 3c: each term is defined again later, and on the second definition the reader 'wondered whether it was a different concept.' The spec's p23 controlling idea requires these one-clause glosses and the forward pointer, so the difficulty comes from the spec's design.

results.quote: The documented lesson from Adevinta Spain's contracts, Vinted's generated tracking code and Adevinta Benelux's metric monitoring, Artemis (described under governed metrics), is the same
results.finding: flow-A 3e: 'forward reference to evidence not yet given.' The spec's p48 does not call for Artemis as evidence here; the draft cites a case the reader meets two sections later. Dropping the Artemis clause (flow-A's suggestion) fixes it without changing the order.

results.draft_locus: Governed Metrics: One Definition of a Contact ¶5
results.quote: The week began on Monday 8 March, the day after Femke listed her bike, so the team replayed the bike's first 24 hours with it.
results.finding: flow-B 3e: most of the bike's first 24 hours fall before the week, so 'so' is a non sequitur; 're-read several times'. flow-B 3f and flow-A 3h: the Golf listed 14 April appears inside the March-week replay and reads as a contradiction until 'added a second example'; the fraud-review aside ('the replay excluded none') slows the paragraph. The spec's order (card, then replay) is fine; the prose packs two time frames into one paragraph with a false causal link.

results.quote: Access policy settles what data may be used; keeping the platform useful and affordable is the remaining work
results.finding: flow-A 3j: 'bridge feels forced; freshness relates more to the consumer table in purpose than to sharing.' flow-B 3j: 'freshness is really an architecture concern arriving after the legal material.' Both call the placement defensible but weak. The bridge sentence does its job; the difficulty is the section's position in the spec's order.

results.draft_locus: Setting the Scene at Veldmark: Three Warehouses, Three Contacts ¶2
results.quote: Tradeyard and Motorvane run Snowflake, in separate accounts with separate models. Hearthly runs BigQuery. Keybridge runs Azure Synapse
results.finding: flow-B 3b: four environments listed against the heading's 'three warehouses', and later 'Most of that bill paid for three separate warehouses' — 'had to recount'. The prose never says which three count (the listing brands' three contact warehouses).

results.draft_locus: Governed Metrics: One Definition of a Contact ¶5
results.quote: Priya's team tested the definition in April, before the forum approved it
results.finding: flow-B 3g: the card approved in May is shown before the April replay that tested it; 'flagged in the text but made the reader check dates.' The order card-then-replay is the spec's (p34 before p37).

results.draft_locus: In Practice: Veldmark's Common Ground Data Platform ¶3
results.quote: The forum had approved the contact definition in May. In September it decided what to deliver first
results.finding: flow-A 3i: the preceding numbered list puts storage first, while delivery put the tracking plan and contact definition first; 'list order differs from delivery order; had to reconcile.' The spec's p52-then-p53 order is fine; one clause saying the list is not the delivery order would remove the friction.

results.draft_locus: Governed Metrics: One Definition of a Contact ¶4
results.quote: **Billing and steering must both be derived from the same contacts data product**
results.finding: flow-A 3g: the billing paragraph 'interrupts the move from card to replay'; flow-A proposes moving it after the replay. The position is the spec's (p36 between p35 and p37).

results.draft_locus: What a Marketplace Data Platform Is For ¶6
results.quote: CDC should be temporary in the data platform too.
results.finding: flow-A 3c: 'returns to a finished point after Figure 1; would sit better after the three-kinds table.' The position (after the join paragraph and its figure) is the spec's order.

Every does_not_know term is defined at or before its first substantive use: data platform (purpose ¶1), tracking plan (tracking ¶1), common envelope (tracking ¶5), data contract/data product/metrics layer (glossed in architecture ¶1, defined later), governed metric (governed metrics ¶1), qualified contact (card), pro data product (pro ¶1), lakehouse/Iceberg/Delta (architecture ¶7), medallion (architecture ¶2), data mesh (data products ¶1), quarantine (architecture ¶3), ePrivacy Art. 5(3) and purpose limitation (tracking ¶6). Callouts preview terms before definition, as previews do. Names flow-B flagged (Sven Lindqvist, Tradeyard's four countries) are on already_knows.
The cold reader named the board question across three warehouses, the four contracts, and all fifteen sections in the roadmap's order, with the expected evidence sources.

The reader builds qualified_contact v1.0 with owner/steward, written definition, server-side delivery count once per buyer and listing, 72-hour fraud restatement, one computation in the metrics layer served to board, experiments and dealer reports, legacy definitions for a quarter, and the bike at 13; refuses the request through purpose-bound access policy (DPO taxonomy, isolation, external audit of policy and log).
